title: 1988 AMC 8 Problem 19
statement: What is the \(100\)th number in the arithmetic sequence \(1,\) \(5,\) \(9,\) \(13,\) \(17,\) \(21,\) \(25,\) \(\ldots?\)

solutions.text:
The sequence starts at \(1\) with common difference \(4.\) The \(100\)th term is reached by adding \(4\) to the first term \(99\) times.

So the \(100\)th term is \(1 + 99 \times 4 = 1 + 396 = 397.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A .
hints: The common difference is \(4,\) so each term adds \(4\) to the previous one
Starting from \(1,\) reaching the \(100\)th term means adding \(4\) a total of \(99\) times
